provenance.purpose: cross-check of vitorino2022.json with a2pm 1.2.0's own (unvectorised) pattern transforms
provenance.settings: library pattern transforms; scikit-learn MLPClassifier (64, 32) without dropout or class weights; attacks of 1 iteration and of at most 50 iterations with early-stopping patience 2

paper: Vitorino, Oliveira & Praca 2022, Adaptative Perturbation Patterns: Realistic Adversarial Learning for Robust Intrusion Detection, Future Internet 14(4):108, doi:10.3390/fi14040108 (arXiv:2203.04234)

paper_results.clean_accuracy_malicious: > 0.99 for both MLP and RF (regular training)
paper_results.targeted_after_1_iteration: accuracy drops by about 15 points (MLP) and 33 points (RF)
paper_results.targeted_after_50_iterations: very low for regular training; RF with adversarial training keeps 0.9991
paper_results.untargeted_regular: accuracy declines by about 99 % and macro-F1 by about 79 % (MLP and RF)
paper_results.untargeted_adv_trained: considerably higher; gradual decrease of < 2 % per iteration

assumptions: MachineLearningCVE Tuesday + Wednesday CSVs (78 numerical features), rows with NaN/inf dropped
Combination pattern on the binary TCP-flag features with Destination Port locked (the paper one-hot encoded categorical features and locked port and protocol)
scikit-learn MLPClassifier (64, 32), no dropout and no class weights (paper: Keras, dropout 0.1, balanced class weights)
A2PM generate: iterations 1 and 50, early-stopping patience 2
